Question: Why is there a need for clothes to be paraded by models?
Answer: One way to look at fashion model shows is to think of the models as bringing life to the garments they’re wearing. By watching the models “parading” you can see how the garments drape on a live person. That helps you visualize how you yourself would look while walking in these same garments. Even if the fashion shows aren’t hosted for the purpose of selling clothing that you would almost never actually wear outdoors, you can still catch a glimpse of many of the style details which eventually show up at your local retail stores. Lately, many retailers (Nordstrom, Macy’s, Chico’s, and plenty more) feature videos of models wearing the clothing they sell directly on their retail sites. Seeing someone modeling an item is a great marketing strategy. Fashion models give you inspiration: “Maybe I can look this nice?” That’s the point of models parading in front of an audience. It’s all part of a marketing program. “Would you like to look this alluring? Stop by Victoria’s Secret!” That’s the concept that answers your question.
